sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stock Photography Marketplace and Generative Visual Assets

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties, including BLEU–China BIT, BLEU–South Korea BIT, and BLEU–Morocco BIT
Luxembourg double taxation agreements (DTAAs) with Germany, France, the United States, and the Netherlands
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement, applicable via Luxembourg's EU membership

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (notably by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 30 August 2019 on RBE operational modalities; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notary of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or utility provider in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / KYC clearance letter for each shareholder and UBO
Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for signature of the Luxembourg notarial deed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP identification and risk classification pursuant to FATF Recommendation 12 and Articles 2 to 5 of the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended. Mandatory list-based screening of all shareholders, directors, managers, and beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, and Luxembourg domestic sanctions lists. OFAC SDN screening is applied as market-standard practice due to correspondent banking and USD clearing requirements. Continuous screening is required on a risk-based frequency: daily for sanctions and periodic (at onboarding and annually) for PEP status.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS electronic portal at https://www.lbr.lu/ (formerly rcs.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be in any language using the Latin script. If the name is not in Luxembourgish, French, or German, an official French or German translation may be required for publication in the RESA. The legal suffix must be in the statutory French form 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'S.à r.l.'. Non-Latin scripts (e.g., CJK, Cyrillic) must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters for the RCS filing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms identical or confusingly similar to existing RCS registrations
Terms contrary to public policy or misleading as to Luxembourg state affiliation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory name reservation register; the 30-day window reflects the operative validity of the LBR name availability check and negative certificate used before notarial signature. Upon name rejection: (1) the applicant may request written reasons from the RCS registrar within 15 days; (2) the applicant may file an administrative complaint with the LBR; (3) if rejected, judicial appeal may be lodged with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within two months of notification, pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and the New Code of Civil Procedure; (4) in parallel, a new name variant may be proposed and cleared for a fresh negative certificate. No statutory extension of the 30-day validation is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as a substitute for a physical registered office in Luxembourg. Domiciliation services are permissible only where the domiciliation provider maintains a genuine physical office in Luxembourg and the SARL can demonstrate intended commercial substance. A mailbox-only virtual office will be rejected by the RCS and by payment intermediaries (Stripe/PayPal) in KYC review. For an ISIC 7420 stock media platform, documentation of IP ownership, bank account, and contractual relationships in Luxembourg is expected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated 10% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a standard-risk digital stock media platform. Inspection probability rises where domiciliation-only substance is used or where revenue volumes materially exceed the declared risk tier. Competent inspection authorities include the RCS, the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD), and law enforcement authorities in AML-linked cases.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS fee schedule; prevailing administrative tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation of SARL (articles of association, intervention minutes, legal formalities)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (Law of 16 December 1991 on notary fees); average market tariff for standard SARL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing and RESA publication (dossier de fondation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing and publication fee, estimated approx. EUR 300

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for initial RBE filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of document origin (Ministry of Foreign Affairs or notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention tariff, USD 10–60 per document; consular legalization surcharge for non-Hague states

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate, approx. USD 80–120 per certified page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business permit / autorisation d'établissement application (manager's commercial license, unless dispensation applies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of the Economy via Guichet.lu

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel pre-incorporation AML/KYC/UBO advisory and document coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for pre-incorporation compliance package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended, Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (S.à r.l. constitution and management); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and annual accounts, Articles 1 to 23; Grand-Ducal Regulation relating to the Luxembourg Business Registers and publication in the electronic compendium.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the supervision of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice; electronic filing through the LBR portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif notarié) comprising the articles of association (statuts), together with the RCS filing form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital for an S.à r.l.; cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least 25% paid up, deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution, with the bank certificate attached to the notarial deed; funds become available to the company only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved at the first shareholders' meeting of S.à r.l. [Company]: 1. Subscription – The share capital of EUR 12,000 is hereby recognized as fully subscribed and paid up per the bank certificate in escrow. 2. Registered Office – The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, in compliance with the articles. 3. Officers – [Name] is appointed sole Manager (Gérant), acting alone, with authority to represent and bind the Company and to execute all registrations. It is further resolved that each resolution takes effect immediately and the Manager shall procure publication and RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit minimum capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g. BIL, Banque Degroof Petercam, Sparkasse) under CSSF supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a Luxembourg bank and present the intended draft articles of association and the KYC file. Instruct the bank to open a blocked account in the name of the future company ('SARL en formation') and transfer at least EUR 12,000 before execution of the incorporation deed. Obtain the bank certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the future company and its notary. Deliver the certificate to the notary before signing. The escrow remains blocked until presentation of the RCS registration extract, after which funds are released to the company's current account.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association or corporate skeleton file
Passport copies and proof of residential address of proposed shareholders and manager
Business description covering ISIC 7420 stock-photography and generative visual asset services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC queries or asks for enhanced due diligence, submit updated identification, clarify the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner, and provide a revised source-of-funds narrative; if delay exceeds the SLA, open an escrow account with a second Luxembourg credit institution and inform the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the selected notary to prepare the final statuts based on the shareholders' decisions and the ISIC 7420 commercial purpose. Present passport copies, bank certificate, powers of attorney if a proxy signs, and the manager's good-conduct declaration. Execute the deed before the notary; the notary reads the deed to the parties, collects signatures, retains the original, and issues certified electronic copies for filing with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of shareholders and manager
Powers of attorney for any representative
Manager acceptance declaration and criminal-record statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistencies in the capital clause, corporate object or officer appointments, execute a supplementary correction deed (acte rectificatif) before filing; no RCS filing is made until the corrected deed is signed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation dossier and obtain RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers electronic filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the notary or an accredited e-filer, upload the notarial deed and the completed RCS registration form into the LBR portal. Pay the applicable state filing fees electronically. The RCS legalization officer examines compliance with the 1915 Companies Act and the RCS law, then allocates the registration number and issues the official extract ('extrait du RCS'). Legal personality arises on registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query for missing or inconsistent data, submit a formal written response together with any notarial correction through the same portal; if already registered, use an RCS rectification filing to cure entry errors without delaying company operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt first board/shareholders resolution and establish corporate governance books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the S.à r.l.; corporate secretary or legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first shareholders' meeting immediately after RCS registration. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office, and appointment of the sole Manager. Prepare formal minutes and insert them into the corporate register. Open the company's operating current account and provide the Manager signature mandate. Create the share register, write the UBO declaration, and file the beneficial-owner return with the Luxembourg Business Registers.
required_dossiers: Shareholder identity documents and share allocations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder contests a resolution, reconvene the meeting with proper statutory notice and adopt an ordinary majority resolution; if the appointed Manager declines office, appoint a substitute Manager by written shareholders' resolution and amend the RCS record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Effect official publication and register for tax and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines (AED); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the RCS to publish the statutory particulars in the electronic compendium, which gives effect against third parties. Apply for the Luxembourg corporate income tax file and VAT number through the official e-filing portal using the RCS extract and statuts. Register the Manager and any employees with the CCSS for social security. Maintain the records of publication confirmation and tax registration references in the governance book.
required_dossiers: Manager identity document and civil status
ISIC 7420 activity description for VAT purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or CCSS queries the registration, resubmit the missing technical data such as authorised signatories, planned commencement date, or commercial address proof; tax registration is declaratory and can be reopened once the file is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete physical workplace and administrative/occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Communal administration of the registered office; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the lease, floor plan and occupancy certificate to the commune for confirmation that the premises are lawfully usable for commercial office activity. Obtain a fire-safety compliance certificate for office occupancy with fewer than 50 persons where required by communal fire protection rules. If employees are engaged, submit the collective workplace declaration to ITM and register the workplace premises. For a pure service company with no industrial installations, no environmental or manufacturing permit is requested.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title for registered office
ITM collective worker and workplace form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commune or ITM issues compliance observations, execute the required structural, electrical or fire-safety works and deliver a technical compliance report; request a re-inspection, normally completed within five working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Directorate of Industry (Direction de l'Industrie), Luxembourg; not applicable to ISIC 7420 service activity unless an establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 is interpreted as applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or environmental manufacturing licence is required for a stock-photography and generative visual asset platform; if implementing a commercial establishment permit, the relevant instrument is the 'autorisation d'établissement' issued by the Ministry of the Economy.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA or registration under the grand-ducal EIA regulation; the activity is an administrative and digital service with no listed industrial installation, no raw-material processing and no emission-generating production process.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission source attributable to the business; general obligations under the Law of 21 June 1976 on environmental protection apply, requiring lawful office waste collection, sorting and disposal through approved municipal operators and compliance with WEEE requirements for electronic office equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification for the registered office covering simple evacuation, smoke detection and electrical fire risk, issued by the communal fire authority or a certified engineering expert. Structural load and occupancy clearance obtained through the commune's occupancy permit for commercial office use. Occupational clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) confirming safe workplace conditions, adequate lighting, ergonomic equipment, and sanitary facilities for administrative staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Unified e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu (Guichet.public.lu); electronic VAT filing via FEDELTAX.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Execute incorporation before a Luxembourg notary and file with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the national business number (matricule, 11-digit numeric) and RCS registration; 2) Register the SARL with the AEDT at the office of the registered seat; 3) Receive VAT identification number formatted LU + 8-digit code derived from the matricule; 4) Non-resident foreign entities must file a direct electronic application to AEDT via the LuxTrust-authenticated MyGuichet portal before commencing taxable activities; no local fiscal agent is statutorily required for EU-resident suppliers, but a tax representative is mandatorily designated by non-EU suppliers without a Luxembourg establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SARL is a capital company fully tax-resident in Luxembourg when its registered office or central administration is in Luxembourg; it is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune), and VAT; no check-the-box pass-through mechanism exists for a SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Art. 164bis LIR for resident companies held at least 95%; 2) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Art. 61 VAT Law; 3) ATAD hybrid mismatch alignment under Art. 168quater LIR imposes mandatory 90-day matching treatment with no elective opt-out for hybrid entities; 4) Small-business VAT exemption election (franchise) under Art. 51(b) VAT Law for annual turnover up to EUR 35,000; 5) IP box deduction under Art. 50bis LIR and participation exemption under Art. 166 LIR require formal economic substance and documentation rather than simple elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Loi du 12 février 1979 and Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-business franchise exemption; no registration threshold for non-established foreign suppliers, registration being compulsory from the first taxable transaction; the EUR 10,000 Union-wide distance-sale/electronic-services threshold applies for intra-EU B2C supplies (above it, destination-state VAT applies via OSS).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping regime in force for B2B/B2C transactions; mandatory B2G e-invoicing from 1 January 2024 (central government) and 1 January 2025 (all public entities) using the PEPPOL network and EN 16931 semantic standard; all VAT returns, recapitulative (EC Sales) statements, and audit files must be filed electronically through FEDELTAX; no national e-invoice clearance API is imposed on private-sector invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods to non-EU destinations are zero-rated under Art. 44 VAT Law upon proof of transport outside the EU; intra-Community supplies to EU taxable persons are zero-rated under Art. 43 VAT Law subject to a valid customer VAT number (VIES) and EC Sales List. For the stock-photo/AI digital asset business, electronically supplied services (image downloads, licensing) follow place-of-supply rules: B2B downloads to EU or non-EU customers are taxed where the customer is established (reverse charge outside Luxembourg), B2C downloads to non-EU consumers fall outside Luxembourg VAT, and B2C downloads to EU consumers are declared through the One-Stop-Shop (Union scheme) at the consumer's country rate. Digital exports require no customs declaration but necessitate robust digital evidence: IP address geolocation, payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) country records, customer contracts, and e-invoice trails.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/IE-507) with Movement Reference Number (MRN) for tangible media shipments
Transport document (Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, Air Waybill, or courier/postal receipt)
Commercial invoice stating 'VAT exempt - export zero-rated Art. 44'
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank/Stripe/PayPal settlement proof evidencing cross-border receipt of funds
Intra-EU supplies: validated customer VAT number extracted from VIES and matching EC Sales List entry
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating is strictly construed and the taxpayer bears the full burden of proof; unsupported or fraudulent claims trigger immediate VAT clawback, monthly arrears interest of 0.8% (Art. 25(2) General Tax Law), administrative fines up to 100% of the evaded tax, and criminal prosecution under Art. 396 General Tax Law (imprisonment and fines up to EUR 250,000); the limitation period extends to 10 years in fraud cases; AEDT systematically cross-checks MRN status, VIES records, PEPPOL invoice data, and payment rail details against FEDELTAX declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting in cooperation with the Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier – CSSF). No dedicated foreign exchange administration exists; Luxembourg maintains full capital-account liberalisation under EU Treaty obligations and eurozone membership, with no exchange-control approval regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg provides unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility for EUR and all foreign currencies pursuant to Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the EU Capital Requirements Regulation framework. Profit remittance is unrestricted; Luxembourg applies a 15% domestic dividend withholding tax, but treaty relief and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may reduce or eliminate it. Outbound interest and royalty payments enjoy no Luxembourg withholding tax, subject to anti-abuse rules and SAAR/GAAR scrutiny. No convertibility hurdles, no advance approvals, and no restrictions on foreign-currency bank accounts apply to a Luxembourg SARL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export receipts. SARLs may retain export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency accounts without repatriation or conversion requirements, consistent with EU free-movement-of-capital principles and Luxembourg's longstanding open-economy policy.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for payment-rail modernisation, but strictly secondary to a full commercial bank. A Luxembourg or EEA-licensed electronic money institution (EMI) or payment institution under PSD2 can be used for multi-currency IBAN collection, currency conversion, and outbound disbursements to photographers and licensees. The EMI must be licensed in Luxembourg or passported under PSD2, maintain segregated client funds, and route settlement through a Tier-1 correspondent bank. EMI accounts are not acceptable for registered capital escrow, notarised capital contribution evidence, or statutory capital compliance because they cannot provide deposit-guarantee-backed operating accounts in the same manner as a credit institution. For a low-risk stock-photo digital platform, a compliant EMI such as Banking Circle or similar EU-licensed provider is viable as a secondary clearance rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally require at least one director or senior natural-person officer to attend an onboarding interview, either physically in Luxembourg or via authenticated video conference using CSSF-compliant remote identification. Remote account opening is permitted in practice only where corporate documents are apostilled, the beneficial-owner structure is fully transparent, and the video KYC is executed according to the EBA Remote Customer Onboarding Guidelines with a qualified electronic signature. For non-resident directors of the SARL, banks typically demand a certified passport copy, proof of residence, and a sworn bank reference from their current banking institution. Physical presence at a bank branch remains the most predictable pathway for a first-tier commercial account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership opacity and source-of-wealth question at account opening for the SARL's subscribed capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised articles of association, Luxembourg RCS extract (Fichier électronique), share register, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, bank statements proving source of initial cash contribution, audited financial statements or an independent accountant's letter, and sworn source-of-wealth affidavits for each shareholder contributing capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border payout model from stock-photo sales triggering suspicion of use as an unlicensed payment intermediary or money-transmission conduit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial model description, customer and photographer agreements, platform terms of service, Stripe/PayPal merchant statements showing gross sales history, ISIC 7420 industry attestation, proof of VAT registration and substance (office lease, payroll, local management), and a board-adopted AML/KYC policy for onboarding freelance contributors and auditing payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI-generated visual-asset IP and royalty flows causing concern over tax-reporting opacity and technological novelty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Inclusive IP assignment agreements, evidence of AI-model licensing or internal research and development records, copyright registration certificates where applicable, patent/design filings, a technical whitepaper explaining the AI generation model, transfer-pricing documentation supporting intercompany remuneration, and tax clearance certificates or correspondence with the Luxembourg Administration de l’enregistrement et des domaines confirming ongoing tax compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The shareholder's capital injection must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT with the narrative 'Capital Increase LU_SARL' and a precise reference to the notarised subscription deed and RCS publication. For EUR, settlement occurs via Target2 through a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank IBAN beginning with 'LU' and representing a BCL participant bank. The bank reconciles the inbound payment with the corporate share register, and the ECB Balance of Payments statistical code 'Direct Investment other capital' (BPM6 DI framework) is applied at reporting. Verification is achieved by the credit's matching the notarised capital-increase resolution, the updated RCS share capital extract, and a bank-issued capital deposit certificate, which is required by the Luxembourg registrar when filing the capital increase.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Low-value royalty distributions to stock-photo contributors are cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer (settlement in T2, EUR-denominated) or SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR accounts and for contributors in countries outside SEPA. High-value exclusive visual-asset purchases use documentary commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by the Luxembourg bank and payable at the seller's confirming bank. For payments to Stripe/PayPal treasury rails, Luxembourg banks use API-based payout files and FX conversion at the bank's wholesale rate, with settlement through correspondent banks and CLS for major FX pairs when netting exposure. The SARL treasury policy must distinguish operating disbursements from intercompany loans and dividends to avoid reclassification as capital movement or hidden profit distribution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forwards with an established commercial bank and board-approved treasury policy
Rolling spot and FX swap contracts not exceeding 12-month forward tenor for working-capital management
Cross-currency basis swaps with an investment-grade EU bank counterparty where a documented foreign-currency liability or asset exists

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible emerging-market currencies, provided a genuine underlying trade invoice exists and the NDF is used solely to hedge settlement risk; EUR/USD NDF is generally not admitted absent a demonstrated regulatory barrier

European vanilla FX options bought (not sold) for asymmetric protection of forecast royalty inflows; option writing is reserved to specialist treasury counterparties under an ISDA/CSA master agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, notes and, where applicable, auditor's report) deposited with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month after shareholder approval and in all cases no later than eight (8) months after the close of the financial year (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit is a criminal offence punishable by fines of EUR 750 to EUR 25,000 (Article 199 of the amended Commercial Code) against the manager(s); continued failure may lead to court-ordered judicial liquidation and administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) of shareholders to approve the annual accounts and grant discharge to the manager(s)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate organ (shareholders' meeting) – no regulatory filing unless the AGM adopts amendments to the articles of association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within six (6) months after the close of the financial year (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the manager(s) fail to convene the AGM, any shareholder may petition the District Court to convoke the meeting; persistent non-compliance exposes the company to judicial liquidation and the manager(s) to civil liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership verification and, where ownership has changed, updated declaration in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual date; any beneficial ownership change must be filed within thirty (30) days of such change; an annual reconciliation of the internal share register against the RBE file is recommended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, inaccurate or omitted RBE filings are subject to administrative fines and criminal penalties of up to EUR 250,000 and/or up to five (5) years' imprisonment (Law of 13 January 2019)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes / réviseur d'entreprises) when it exceeds, for two consecutive financial years, two of the three following thresholds: (a) balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, (b) net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and (c) average workforce of 50 employees (Article 65-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915; Law of 23 July 2016 on the audit profession). The ISIC 7420 stock-photo marketplace entity, operated at an ordinary low-risk level, will generally remain below these thresholds and hence outside the compulsory audit regime.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Minimal Normalisé) pursuant to the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register, accounting and annual accounts of undertakings; consolidated accounts, if any, may be prepared under IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL is required to keep an accurate, up-to-date file at the RBE identifying every ultimate beneficial owner (natural persons holding, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of shares or voting rights). No statutory annual blanket re-filing is imposed; however, any transfer of shares or change in the beneficial ownership structure must be notified to the RBE within 30 days. The manager(s) must perform an annual verification of the internal shareholder register against the RBE record, retain supporting documentation, and promptly update the RBE upon any modification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of Shareholders' Meetings and of Manager Resolutions
RBE beneficial-ownership documentation and supporting evidence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - USD 4,500 per annum (EUR 1,500 - EUR 4,000), covering registered office provision, statutory agent, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 12,000 per annum (EUR 2,500 - EUR 10,000) for a full statutory audit of a small to mid-size SARL; USD 1,500 - USD 3,000 (EUR 1,200 - EUR 2,500) for a voluntary independent review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective rate for Luxembourg City (17% national corporate income tax plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the national CIT, yielding 18.19%, plus 6.75% municipal business tax). Rates vary slightly by commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for commercial stock-photo or AI visual-asset platforms. Applicable incentives include: (i) an 80% exemption for qualifying intellectual-property income under the Luxembourg IP box, producing an effective rate of approximately 5%; (ii) a refundable R&D tax credit on eligible software and AI research expenditure; (iii) a notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity; and (iv) an investment tax credit for certain capital expenditure. Losses may be carried forward without a finite statutory cap, subject to anti-loss-trafficking rules and continuity of activity; loss carry-back is not permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 880 (combined annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return) filed electronically through the eCDF extranet of the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD), authenticated via MyGuichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; separate mandatory quarterly prepayment declarations for corporate income tax and municipal business tax are due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September, and 10 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the Form 880 filing deadline is 31 December of the year following the tax year. For a non-calendar financial year, filing is due within six months after the balance-sheet date. A mandate to a registered Luxembourg tax adviser extends the deadline to 30 April of the second year following the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, RCS number, LEI/electronic entity identifier, registered office, tax file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL must use its full Luxembourg RCS identifier; foreign parent and ultimate beneficial owner details are inserted in the shareholder annex, not in Box 1a.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual financial statements under Luxembourg GAAP: balance sheet, profit and loss account, and annexes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent must attach a consolidated group presentation if transfer pricing documentation is triggered; no foreign statutory audit copy is accepted without Luxembourg Annexe translation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before deductions: accounting profit adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, and tax timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL is resident and taxed on worldwide income; foreign-source income derived by the SARL from stock-photo sales and AI licensing must be included unless covered by a specific exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions claimed: participation exemption on substantial shareholdings, IP-box exemption on qualifying AI/software royalties, notional interest deduction, and R&D tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot deduct Luxembourg-company losses against foreign tax returns merely because the SARL is transparent; the SARL is a separate taxable entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax loss utilisation: losses carried forward from earlier tax periods subject to continuity and anti-abuse conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward claims must be supported by prior notices of assessment; non-resident directors must preserve loss records and ownership continuity schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: 17% national CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge, and communal municipal business tax at the applicable commune rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Municipal business tax is levied on the Luxembourg business establishment; no non-resident establishment is required, but the SARL's Luxembourg place of effective management is decisive.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing declaration and related-party transaction schedule, including cross-border licensing, service fees, and financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must disclose every related-party transaction with the foreign parent or affiliates; the ACD may require a Local File even below the documentation threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax declaration: taxable net wealth on Luxembourg-situated assets, exemptions, and wealth-tax prepayment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commercial stock-photo companies generally remain subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax on assets above EUR 500,000 after the statutory allowance; foreign-owned stock photo IP may fall within Luxembourg situs rules if legally registered or exploited through the SARL.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 880 attracts a late-filing penalty of up to EUR 2,500, with repeat violations or concealment increasing the penalty to EUR 25,000. Under-declared tax attracts a 10% late-payment surcharge plus monthly late interest at 0.6%. Criminal tax evasion can lead to imprisonment and fines up to EUR 50,000 or more. Directors who knowingly fail to remit taxes can be held jointly and severally liable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders. A 0% rate applies to a qualifying corporate shareholder under the Luxembourg Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation when the shareholder holds at least 10% of share capital or an acquisition price of EUR 1.2 million for an uninterrupted 12-month period. Non-resident portfolio shareholders not entitled to treaty relief remain subject to the 15% final withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A shareholder seeking DTA relief must submit to the ACD either a pre-payment application for tax relief at source or a subsequent reclaim. Required documents: home-jurisdiction tax residency certificate (TRC) confirming beneficial ownership, a holding-attestation for at least 12 months, and treaty entitlement forms. Dividend distributions to non-resident individuals or entities within the DTA network are commonly reduced to 5% at a 10% shareholding threshold or 0% at a higher participation threshold, depending on the applicable treaty. Refund claims must generally be filed within five years from the year of withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg law imposes no withholding tax on royalties or interest paid to non-residents. Consequently, arm's-length royalty payments for AI-generated stock imagery and software licences, and interest paid on shareholder loans, are not subject to Luxembourg source WHT. The Luxembourg DTA network generally confirms a 0% source-tax rate for interest and royalties. If a treaty or domestic-law annex requires a certificate, the TRC must be exchanged before payment to prevent any administrative blockage.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 in aggregate related-party transactions during a tax year: a formal Local File must be prepared and held available for the ACD; a Master File is required when the worldwide group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000. A mandatory transfer-pricing declaration in Form 880 is due for any related-party transaction exceeding EUR 100,000. The ACD may always request contemporaneous evidence even below these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to the Caribbean-style ESR, but the economic-substance doctrine operates through the general anti-abuse rule (article 6 LIR), EU anti-tax-avoidance directives, and administrative practice. An AI stock-photo SARL must demonstrate real presence and activity in Luxembourg: local strategic management, office premises, employee decision-making on IP exploitation, risk monitoring, and adequate payroll. Insufficient substance exposes the taxpayer to denial of the IP box, DTA relief, dividends-received exemption, and VAT recovery, as well as recharacterisation of royalty income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and false tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of stock-photo licensing royalties or AI-generated visual asset income from Form 880; creation of false invoices; expense padding through fictitious content-production vendors; supplying false statements to the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD reassesses taxable income and applies late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, a 10% late-payment penalty, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000, and criminal fines up to EUR 50,000 or more. Active concealment can prosecute principals under Luxembourg tax-fraud criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or divert corporate assets may have the corporate veil pierced. Courts impose joint and several liability for unpaid tax and restitution, asset freezes, travel bans, and imprisonment for up to five years in aggravated fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation failure and artificial profit stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare Local File or Master File; paying excessive royalty or licence fees to a low-tax foreign AI holding entity; using undocumented intercompany loans; omitting the transfer-pricing declaration in Form 880; applying an unsupported profit split to AI training-data costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD can adjust taxable income to the arm's-length result, deny tax deductions, impose interest and a 10% surcharge, and apply administrative penalties for missing documentation up to EUR 25,000. Tax reassessment statutes generally run for five years but extend to ten years in cases of fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute artificial TP structures can be held personally liable for gross management fault and restitution. Civil courts may freeze personal assets and issue travel bans; criminal prosecution for tax evasion can result in imprisonment and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company structure and sham economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL as a letterbox entity: no real employees, no registered office substance, no board meetings in Luxembourg, no operational risk control, and registered IP in Luxembourg solely to exploit the 80% IP-box exemption without business reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD applies the general anti-abuse rule and recharacterises transactions; the IP-box exemption, participation exemption, and treaty benefits are denied; tax assessments are reopened for previous years; penalties of up to EUR 12,500 plus interest apply. Compulsory liquidation may be sought for untrue declarations of seat and activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and passive directors are exposed to piercing the corporate veil: joint liability for suppressed Luxembourg tax, disgorgement of management fees, travel bans, and asset seizure orders. Criminal courts may impose imprisonment for abuse of corporate vehicles in a cross-border tax arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding-tax evasion on dividends and shareholder distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to foreign shareholders without withholding the 15% dividend tax; applying the 0% parent-subsidiary exemption without verifying the 10% holding period; distributing profits through disguised shareholder loans or excessive management charges to avoid dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD recovers unpaid withholding tax without a time bar in cases of fraud, plus monthly interest of 0.6%, a 10% late-payment surcharge, and penalties up to EUR 25,000. The Luxembourg tax claim becomes a priority claim over corporate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors are personally liable as tax collectors for withheld but unremitted dividend tax. Courts may order personal civil restitution, property attachment, travel bans, and imprisonment for misappropriation of withheld amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/KYC failures in cross-border payment rail operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Stripe and PayPal payment rails without a documented AML compliance framework, failing to perform customer and seller due diligence, using shell payment accounts for stock-photo sellers, or processing transactions from sanctioned or high-risk counterparties while being classified as low AML risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML/CFT sanctions impose administrative penalties scaled to turnover, entity-level fines up to EUR 1,250,000, revocation of financial-sector authorisations where applicable, and imprisonment of up to five years for laundering funds derived from tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers can be personally fined and banned from management duties for up to five years. Civil liability extends to compensating aggrieved payers; travel bans and freezing orders may be imposed while criminal proceedings are pending.
